'''George Turner''' (born 9 August 1940) is a British [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] politician.

==Early life==
{{unreferencedsect|date=October 2026}}
Turner attended Laxton Grammar School (now part of [[Oundle School]]) on North Street in [[Oundle]]. At [[Imperial College London]] he gained a [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] in Physics, then obtained a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in Physics from [[Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge]]. He then became Head of the Electrical Engineering Department at the [[University of East Anglia]].

==Parliamentary career==
Turner contested [[North West Norfolk (UK Parliament constituency)|North West Norfolk]] on behalf of Labour in 1992, but failed to be elected. He was returned as the [[Member of Parliament (United Kingdom)|member of parliament]] (MP) for the constituency in 1997, but lost his seat back to [[Henry Bellingham (Norfolk MP)|Henry Bellingham]] of the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] – whom he had first defeated – in 2001.

In defeating Bellingham in 1997, Turner benefitted from a somewhat curious echo of a famous historical episode, as noted by the Conservative peer and historian [[Alistair Cooke, Baron Lexden|Lord Lexden]] during a debate in the [[House of Lords]] in 2012. Referring to [[Spencer Perceval]], the only Prime Minister to have been assassinated, Lexden remarked in that debate: "My Lords, would my noble friend think of reminding Mr Henry Bellingham that he has already experienced the Perceval family's taste for revenge, having been deprived of his Commons seat at the 1997 election by a direct descendant of the assassinated Prime Minister?"<ref>Hansard Parliamentary Debates, [https://hansard.parliament.uk/Lords/2012-04-25/debates/12042545000859/SpencerPerceval#contribution-12042545000024 "Spencer Perceval"], volume 736, column 1786, 25 April 2012.</ref> Perceval's descendant was a third candidate in the constituency, Roger Percival of the [[Referendum Party]], who in Lexden's view had deprived Bellingham (in turn a kinsman of Spencer Perceval's assassin, [[John Bellingham]], and thus a suitable target for "revenge") of a critical number of votes in the election, thereby delivering victory to George Turner.

==Personal life==
{{unreferencedsect|date=October 2026}}
He married Lesley Duggan. He has two daughters a stepson and stepdaughter.
